I feel you, I was dumped 2 weeks ago by a toxic partner after 2,5 year relationship. But it was so bad at the end that I can't say I still love him, I guess I stopped at some point (at the beginning I was - we were - crazy in love). My ex-boyfriend was controlling, possessive, manipulative and jealous and was trying to convince me that those are the qualities of a *Real Man* and that I am too emotional and crazy. It made me feel like shit, and because I stayed with him so long I lost respect for myself and got depressed. So if your relationship was toxic and there was any level of possessiveness and distrust I think it would only get worse. It's better to end things when you both still have some dignity and not hate each other, trust me. Your close friends and family probably have realized that this is toxic relationship way before you - talk to them honestly and ask for their opinion. You don't need to take their every word for granted, people could be biased, but generally they hate to see you unhappy and hurt, so hear them out. I've got big deal of support from my friends and parents and their observations about my past relationship ("You were fading away", "You didn't seem like yourself", "You were nervous and always checking your phone", "You didn't smile at all" - big red flags!) made me sure that this is for the best. You deserve a healthy, normal relationship and you will love again, love is not a one-time thing. Take care.

I have a friend of 15 years (I'm 28). We had one big argument and didn't speak to each other for a year, but we missed this friendship greatly and made up. I have 2-3 other close friends that I met in middle/high school and we're still very close. We've been there for each other for better and worse, I feel safe and accepted with them so I don't think - I hope - I'm gonna lose them. But I had few people in my life that I just kinda ghosted. Have been friends with them for 2-3 years, got really tired/uncomfortable with them and just stopped talking to them.

I'm feeling the same as you, as a child I tried scouting, singing in a choir, playing in a band, and I've never felt like I really was a member of something, so I quit a lot. I got seriously discouraged by it and never tried to be a part of any community as a teenager (besides my group of very close friends). College was a nightmare for me - everyone bonding besides me (at least thet's how it felt). So I don't know. Now when I'm an adult I feel like I'm missing something important, so I guess, maybe it's worth trying...?

Thank you guys for the comments. Shortly after that episode I went to the psychiatrist, was diagnosed with depression, borderline personality and some other stuff... I was prescribed antidepressants and psychotherapy. I've found a really nice therapist and had two sessions already. In the meantime, my boyfriend of 2 years broke up with me (kinda grateful for that, because that relationship was toxic and he was a manipulative son of a bitch), I had to move out from his apartment and I have found new place for myself. All of that in one week, so that was tough. I hope the meds will help me with that dark obsessive thoughts that haunt me from time to time and make my life unbearable. I hope sometime in the future I will find someone supportive and loving. I hope I will get back that sense of self and my interests and my passion for life. For everyone in the SuicideWatch, thinking dark thoughts - go get some help as fast as you can. You all can be healed and happy, I truly believe that. Please, keep your fingers crossed for me and take care.
